answer_1.quote: Our method leverages prosodic features (pitch, energy and duration) to modify emotions in the output of a TTS system. ... The backbone has three modules; an encoder, variance adaptor and decoder. The encoder maps an input phoneme sequence to its embedding. ... The decoder returns Mel-spectrogram frames that are converted to speech.
datasets: Theatre dialogue segments from Speed-the-Plow, Night, Mother, Bobby Gould in Hell, Death of a Salesman
answer_1.outputs: Synthetic speech audio (Mel‑spectrograms rendered to waveform via vocoder)

answer_4.quote: We compare Mean Opinion Score (MOS) averaged across forty subjects proficient in English. ... Annotator rates each sample on a Likert scale of one for 'completely unnatural' to five for 'completely natural'. ... In the first survey, given a sample, we ask the user to choose the best perceived emotion from a set of four ... In the second survey we evaluate the efficacy of the models to bring about finer control over emotion ... Forty raters rank the three settings in terms of emotional consistency of the dialogue ... The closeness of Actor M's behavior to this reference while interacting with the two TTS models is used as a measure of the latter's effectiveness.
answer_4.guideline: Rate naturalness on a 1‑5 Likert scale; select perceived emotion (Happy, Sad, Angry, Fear); identify which of two samples shows higher arousal intensity; rank conversation settings by emotional consistency; evaluate actor's behavioral response using Pearson correlation and arousal statistics.
